## p92 A — Dutch courier Vreede's passage to Constantinople

**Sources on this page:** p92 A. [Concise case study](../people/p92_A.md).

<a id="edition-cases-people-p92-a-p92-a--dutch-courier-vreedes-passage-to-constantinople"></a>


[ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [All readings](../README.md) · [Source certificate](../../experiments/corpus_recovery/certificates.json) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Record:** p92 A, 1 November 1918, addressed in clear to the Political
Section at Bucharest. **Result:** all **214 plaintext positions** are fixed
from **428 unchanged source coordinates** with the published Nov1–3 key.
One explicit coordinate substitution gives the readable text below.

<a id="edition-cases-people-p92-a-reading"></a>

### Reading

**Readable German:**

> Nr. 607. Bitte dafuer zu sorgen, dass niederlaendischer Kurier,
> Rittmeister Vreede, der mit unserem COSPOLI-Kurier zusammen am 3.11.
> hier abfaehrt, in Braila mit dem Schiff nach Konstantinopel
> mitgenommen wird. Auswaertiges Amt. 1. 41362.

**Meaning:** The Foreign Office asks the Political Section to arrange for
the Dutch courier, Rittmeister Vreede, to be taken aboard the ship from
Braila to Constantinople. He is to leave the sender's location on
3 November together with its `COSPOLI` courier.

The surname **VREEDE**, rank, nationality, **607**, **3.11**, Braila,
Constantinople and closing **1 / 41362** all come directly from unchanged
source coordinates. The text does not identify Vreede by first name.
`COSPOLI` is retained as transmitted, and the source does not itself name
the location meant by “here.” Spacing, punctuation and capitalization are
editorial.

<a id="edition-cases-people-p92-a-source-and-one-repair"></a>

### Source and one repair

The [source image](../../experiments/corpus_recovery/sources/p92_A.png) reads:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
UKS v LP (8.25 p.m., November 1st)
1730 (1/11) POLITISCHE ABTEILUNG BUKAREST
RICHI-428?
```

</details>

The question mark after the advertised length is literally printed; the
body contains exactly **428 valid coordinates**. Its fifteenth group is
clearly `VVVFG`. The earlier OCR's shorter `V?FG` is not used as a source
transcription or repaired by inventing a historical coordinate.

The direct raw decipherment is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
NRX607XBITTEDAFUERZUSORGENXDASSNIEDERLAENDISCHERKURIERXRITTMEISTERXVREEDEXDERMITUNSEREMXCOSPOLIXKURIERZUSAMM7NAMX3X11XHIERABFAEHRTXINXBRAILAXMITDEMSCHIFFNACHXKONSTANTINOPELXMITGENOMMENWIRDXAUSWAERTIGESAMTX1X41362XX
```

</details>

Only **`ZUSAMM7N → ZUSAMMEN`** is proposed. It costs one source-coordinate
change, zero-based index **123: F→V**. The candidate preserves the other
**427** coordinates, changes no length or key, and re-encrypts exactly to
that explicitly repaired source.

<a id="edition-cases-people-p92-a-reproduction-and-credit"></a>

### Reproduction and credit


System*, printed p92 / PDF p95 in the
[public scan](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).

Source inspection and this annotated edition: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.
No first historical decipherment priority is claimed.

## Orient intelligence: expected landings and fighting on the Tigris

**Sources on this page:** p92 B1. [Concise case study](../military/orient_intelligence.md).

**Shared edition.** The following reading also discusses [p93 A2](093.md#source-p93-a2), [p93 A3](093.md#source-p93-a3), [p93 A4](093.md#source-p93-a4), [p94 A5](094.md#source-p94-a5), [p94 A6](094.md#source-p94-a6).

<a id="edition-cases-military-orient-intelligence-orient-intelligence-expected-landings-and-fighting-on-the-tigris"></a>



**Source:** J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*,
printed p92 B1, p93 A2–A4 and p94 A5–A6; PDF pp95–97.
**Edition:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.

These six numbered parts share `OSM v LP (4.20 p.m., November 1st)`,
the clear addressee `SSD DEUTSCHER N O OSM OHL ZUGL FUER UNTERST N O`,
and the origin line `(1/11) 0415 6 TEILE`. The final plaintext signature
is `ABT FREMDE HEERE`. Their [source edition](../../experiments/orient_intelligence/README.md)
contains every literal coordinate and exact repair.

The report first corrects an earlier Orient note, then assesses reports
of shipping and expected landings around Alexandretta. It ends with an
English-reported attack against Turkish positions near `KALAT SHERGAT`
and a qualified claim about British cavalry. The source presents
observations, assessments and allegations; this edition preserves those
distinctions.

<a id="edition-cases-military-orient-intelligence-p92-b1"></a>

### p92 B1

The source advertises and prints **328 valid coordinates**. Its raw body is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
DEUTSCQERNOOSMOHLZUGLFUERUNTERSTNOXBERICHTIGUNGZUVORTRXNOTORIENTVOMX30X10X2ABSATZSYRIENXMUSSAMSCHLUSSHEISSENXALSOANSCHEINENDX7XINDXDIVX60XGEMXDIVXODEDXFALLSX54XUSWX
```

</details>

The candidate repairs `DEUTSCQER` to `DEUTSCHER` and `ODED` to `ODER`:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
DEUTSCHERNOOSMOHLZUGLFUERUNTERSTNOXBERICHTIGUNGZUVORTRXNOTORIENTVOMX30X10X2ABSATZSYRIENXMUSSAMSCHLUSSHEISSENXALSOANSCHEINENDX7XINDXDIVX60XGEMXDIVXODERXFALLSX54XUSWX
```

</details>

This costs **three observed-coordinate substitutions**. The clear
header independently contains `DEUTSCHER`. The report calls itself a
correction to the Orient presentation note of raw `30 X 10`, second
paragraph on Syria, and says the ending should read:

**Readable German:**

> Also anscheinend 7 X IND X DIV X 60 X GEM X DIV X oder X falls X 54 X usw.

Those unit labels and the fragmentary syntax are preserved. The earlier
note is not supplied or reconstructed from this correction alone.

<a id="edition-cases-military-orient-intelligence-p93-a2"></a>

### p93 A2

The source advertises and prints **252 coordinates**. Earlier OCR merged
this part with A3 and A4; applying the printed boundary gives the
following complete **126-position raw reading**, without any edit:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
VORTRAGSNOTIZENX31X10X1918XORIENTROEMX1XSYRIENBEVORSTEHENDELANDUNGINALEXANDRETTENACHFLIEGERMELUNGVOM29X10FUHREINGELEITZUGVONX2
```

</details>

This is headed presentation notes, raw `31 X 10 X 1918`, Orient,
`ROEM X 1`, Syria: an expected landing at Alexandretta. It attributes a
convoy report to an air observation of raw `29 X 10`. The received
`FLIEGERMELUNG` is left intact; an apparent omitted `D` is not inserted
into the ciphertext.

<a id="edition-cases-military-orient-intelligence-p93-a3"></a>

### p93 A3

The source advertises and prints **394 valid coordinates**. The
**197-position raw reading** is complete and unchanged:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
GROESZERENTRANSPORTERN1KREUZERXUX4XTORPEDOBOOTENX40XKMXSUEDWESTLXALEXANDRETTEINFAHRTRICHTUNGALEXANDRETTEAUSZERDEMWURDEINDERBUCHTVONXARSUSXEINGROSZESSCHIFFBEOBACHTETNACHALLDENMELDUNGENDERLETZTENTAGE
```

Continuing A2, the report describes larger transports with a cruiser and
torpedo boats southwest of Alexandretta, heading toward it, and another
large ship observed in the bay of the received place name `ARSUS`.
The raw convoy and distance labels `2`, `1`, `4` and `40 X KM` are
unchanged. The `SZ` spellings in `GROESZEREN`, `AUSZERDEM` and `GROSZES`
are kept as received. `XARSUSX` has its surrounding separators; no
geographical letter is supplied from a modern map.

<a id="edition-cases-military-orient-intelligence-p93-a4"></a>

### p93 A4

The source advertises and prints **328 valid coordinates**. Its
**164-position direct reading** is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
UEBERGESTEIGERTENSCHIFFVERKEHRVORDERXSYRISCHENXKUESTEUNDDERTAETIGKEITDERAUFKLAERUNGSFAHRZEUGEVORXALEXANDRETTEXMUSSMITUNMITTELBARBEVORSTEHENDENLANDUNGSVERSUCHENINDER
```

</details>

It continues the assessment that, given recent reports of increased
shipping off the Syrian coast and reconnaissance vessels near
Alexandretta, imminent landing attempts should be expected. This is a
forecast within the source. The text does not say that such a landing
had already occurred.

Parts A2–A4 together have **974 source coordinates and 487 plaintext
positions**. Earlier OCR treated them as one 977-slot stream. Their
three correctly separated readings each re-encrypt exactly to the
unchanged observed source.

<a id="edition-cases-military-orient-intelligence-p94-a5"></a>

### p94 A5

The source advertises **368 slots**, with one printed dash in its first
group, `GDGV-`. Its raw reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
BUCHTVONALEXANDRETTEXGERECHNETWERDENXROEMX2?MESOPOTAMIENX7NGLISCHERVORMARSCHAMXTIGRISXNACHENGLORIENTBERICHTGRIFFENENGLISCHETRUPPENAMX29X10XDIETUERKISCHENSTELLUNGENNOERDLXKALATXSHERGATX
```

</details>

The candidate is:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
BUCHTVONALEXANDRETTEXGERECHNETWERDENXROEMX2XMESOPOTAMIENXENGLISCHERVORMARSCHAMXTIGRISXNACHENGLORIENTBERICHTGRIFFENENGLISCHETRUPPENAMX29X10XDIETUERKISCHENSTELLUNGENNOERDLXKALATXSHERGATX
```

</details>

It fills the printed dash at source index **4** with **X** and changes
source index **44 F→V**, repairing `7NGLISCHER`. All other coordinates
are preserved, including the raw section and date labels. The source
forms `VXFXG` and `XDXFF` also correct earlier OCR, directly restoring
the complete words `ALEXANDRETTE` and `TRUPPEN` without source edits.

The opening completes the expectation of landing attempts in the bay
of Alexandretta. The next section is Mesopotamia: English advance on
the Tigris. According to an English Orient report, troops attacked
Turkish positions north of the received `KALAT X SHERGAT` on raw
`29 X 10`. The text's attribution to another report remains explicit.

<a id="edition-cases-military-orient-intelligence-p94-a6"></a>

### p94 A6

All **350 coordinates** are observed. The full **175-position raw text**
needs no repair:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
ANUNDDRANGENNACHHEFTIGENANSCHEINENDSCHWERENKAEMPFENINDIESTELLUNGENEINTEILEDERTUERKENDIEZUENTKOMMENVERSUCHTENWURDENANGEBLICHDURCHBRITISCHEKAVALLERIEABGESCHNITTENXABTFREMDEHEERE
```

**Readable German — continuation of A5; the leading ellipsis does not mark a missing position in A6:**

> … an und drangen nach heftigen, anscheinend schweren Kämpfen in die Stellungen ein. Teile der Türken, die zu entkommen versuchten, wurden angeblich durch britische Kavallerie abgeschnitten. Abt. Fremde Heere.

`ANSCHEINEND` and `ANGEBLICH` are fully observed and retained. The report
is not presented as independent confirmation of the severity of the
fighting or the cavalry claim.

<a id="edition-cases-military-orient-intelligence-attribution-and-verification"></a>

### Attribution and verification

The unchanged Nov1–3 square and ranks are previously published.
Parts one, five and six also predate this edition as readable unreviewed
repository candidates. The incorrectly merged p93 candidate was
unreadable; its exact prior output is frozen in the inputs. The new
contribution is the source transcription, separated part frames,
complete report assembly and reversible repairs.

The Lasry et al. paper and dissertation discuss Foreign Armies
intelligence generally. The bounded check did not locate an explicit
discussion of this six-part body, and the cached comment-thread check
found no such body. That does not establish decipherment priority.

The six records contain **2,020 printed slots**, **2,019 valid coordinates**
and **1,010 plaintext positions**. There are **1,009 fixed raw positions**;
the explicit candidates fix all 1,010 at a total cost of **four observed
substitutions and one printed-erasure fill**. No key, rank or source
length is changed. All dates, unit numbers, convoy figures and distance
labels are unchanged, while the separately repaired raw `7` in
`7NGLISCHER` remains visible in the audit.

```bash
python experiments/orient_intelligence/verify.py --verify
python experiments/orient_intelligence/verify.py --verify --pdf /path/to/childs.pdf
```
